rationale: The buyer is a developer or IT admin at a company building M365/Teams integrations — a nameable professional with budget authority who already pays for tools. Willingness to pay is moderate: no direct paid competitor was cited, though the ecosystem (Azure Marketplace tools, consulting) confirms some spend. Operational autonomy passes the floor at 7 — a self-serve configuration validator can run fully automated — but responsiveness_signal is untested and the total falls below the 6.5 build threshold, so validate is the right stage. The core risk is whether developers will pay for this versus using Microsoft's own (free but bad) documentation.
solution_plan: This is a self-serve Microsoft Graph permissions configurator: you describe your integration goal in plain English (e.g. 'send Teams messages as a user, read employee directory'), and the tool outputs the exact permission scopes needed, whether app or delegated, and a step-by-step Azure AD setup checklist. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt pipeline behind a simple web form (no coding by Youval), with a Stripe payment link for a one-time report ($19–$39) or a monthly seat ($29/mo for teams). Sell by posting targeted answers on StackOverflow and ServerFault threads where this exact pain appears, linking to a free 'permission checker' with an upsell — outreach batches go out only after Youval approves. Delivery is fully automated: form submission triggers Claude to generate the report PDF/HTML, emailed automatically. The only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing Stripe payouts. Caveat: Microsoft's Graph documentation is improving, so validate demand before building.
notes: build_gate willingness_to_pay is borderline (scored 5, exactly at floor). Total 6.0 is below min_total_to_build (6.5). Validate first with a free landing page and a waitlist or single paid pilot.
